chunks: As for what al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from al-Nadr, from 'Abd Allah ibn Sinan, who said:

Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام said: Allah, Most High, has made obligatory in the salat (prayer) the ruku' (bowing) and the sujud (prostration). Do you not see that if a man were to enter Islam and not be able to recite the Qur'an well, it would suffice him to say the takbir, perform tasbih, and pray?

Thus, the proper way regarding this report is that we interpret it as applying to one who does not recite Fatihat al-Kitab well, in accordance with what it contains. And his statement, "Allah has made obligatory in the salat (prayer) the ruku' (bowing) and the sujud (prostration)," means an obligation such that if he leaves them deliberately or forgetfully, he must repeat the salat (prayer), because they are two pillars. The recitation is not like that, because one who forgets the recitation until he has entered into ruku' (bowing) is not required to repeat the salat (prayer). So the difference between them is from this perspective.

key_terms.الرُّكُوعَ: the bowing position in salat (prayer), treated here as a pillar
key_terms.السُّجُودَ: the prostration in salat (prayer), treated here as a pillar
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: the prescribed salat (prayer) being discussed in legal terms
key_terms.الْقُرْآنَ: the Qur'an, whose recitation may be excused for one unable to perform it
key_terms.الْقِرَاءَةُ: the recitation within salat (prayer), distinguished from the pillars
key_terms.رُكْنَانِ: two pillars whose omission necessitates repetition of the prayer
key_terms.فَاتِحَةَ الْكِتَابِ: Surah al-Hamd, the Opening of the Book, referred to as the recitation in question

ai.seo_question: If someone cannot recite Surah al-Hamd in salat (prayer), is the prayer still valid?
ai.summary: This report distinguishes between essential pillars of salat (prayer), such as ruku' (bowing) and sujud (prostration), and recitation, which does not carry the same ruling in every case. It also indicates that a new Muslim who cannot yet recite the Qur'an is excused and may perform takbir and tasbih in prayer instead.
